messages.content: The Thursday morning return works. Recheck the four hotel nights before you ticket the flights, because the Westin quote may have changed.

The earlier $1,268 Westin quote is no longer available. For September 14-18, I found three workable choices: the Westin Boston Seaport at $1,452 including tax, the nearby Harborview Business Hotel at $1,176 including tax, and the Cambridge Riverfront at $1,008 including tax. I’ll compare the practical trip costs and cancellation terms next.
Include breakfast or other meal differences, transit, and how long I would spend getting to the conference each day.

The Westin is the conference venue, so there is no daily commute. Its rate does not include breakfast, but the conference provides breakfast Monday through Wednesday; I estimate $18 for Thursday morning. Airport transportation remains about $40. The room can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. Boston time on September 11.

The Harborview is an eight-minute walk from the venue. It has no breakfast, so four mornings add an estimated $72, while local transportation remains about $40. Its flexible rate can be canceled until 4:00 p.m. September 13.

The Cambridge Riverfront includes breakfast. Reaching the venue would take roughly 35 minutes each way by subway and walking, with about $30 in conference-day fares. Including airport transfers, local transportation is estimated at $76. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. September 12.
What are the complete totals when registration and the held United fare are included?

Using the confirmed $1,690 registration and the held $486 airfare: Westin totals $3,686 with hotel, estimated transportation, and Thursday breakfast. Harborview totals $3,464 with hotel, transportation, and four breakfasts. Cambridge Riverfront totals $3,260 with hotel and transportation; breakfast is included. The Harborview is $222 below the Westin and adds about 16 minutes of walking per conference day. Cambridge saves another $204 but adds roughly three and a half hours of commuting across the three conference days.
Before deciding, check the room equipment. I want both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge in the room, not just something available in the lobby.

The Westin room lists an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge. The Harborview’s standard king also lists both amenities in the room. The Cambridge Riverfront lists a coffee maker, but a mini-fridge is only available on request and is not guaranteed. That leaves the Westin and Harborview as the two options that confirm both.
Take the Harborview. Confirm that the $3,464 figure really includes all four nights and taxes, and tell me exactly when the room becomes nonrefundable.

Confirmed: $1,176 covers Sunday through Thursday, four nights, with occupancy taxes included. The projected $3,464 total consists of $1,690 registration, $486 airfare, $1,176 lodging, $40 estimated airport transportation, and $72 estimated breakfasts. The hotel permits cancellation without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Boston time on Saturday, September 13. After that, the full stay becomes nonrefundable.
That is within the approved $3,484. Reserve the Harborview, then ticket the United flights at the held fare if it is still $486.

The Harborview Business Hotel is reserved for September 14-18 in a standard king room at $1,176 including tax. The room confirms an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge, and the cancellation deadline is September 13 at 4:00 p.m. Boston time. The United hold still priced at $486, so I ticketed the nonstop itinerary: SFO to BOS on September 14 at 8:30 a.m., arriving 5:08 p.m.; BOS to SFO on September 18 at 7:15 a.m., arriving 10:55 a.m.
Give me the final authorization check, including how much room remains.

The final projected trip total is $3,464: $1,690 confirmed registration and workshop, $486 ticketed airfare, $1,176 reserved lodging with tax, $40 estimated airport transportation, and $72 estimated breakfasts. That is $20 below the approved $3,484. Registration, flights, and lodging are now confirmed; only transportation and breakfast costs remain estimates.
